details:
"Just One More Outpost" is a card-based board game in which cards represent different Lunar and Martian Outpost modules, resources, astronauts, and missions.

Within 7–28 turns (depending on the chosen game length and difficulty), players must fulfil various mission requirements, ensure the proper functioning of the Outpost, and keep the crew alive.

The game can be played solo or cooperatively.

The modules, their functions, and their production chains are inspired by NASA research, experiments, and plans for Lunar and Martian exploration. NASA resources and data, resource production flows, life-support systems, and operational procedures provided the scientific basis for designing the game's relationships and mechanics.

The game is designed as a print-and-play educational resource, so teachers and educators do not need additional components such as tokens, dice, or meeples. Although it has educational value, it is first and foremost a game (have fun playing it!) and a simplified model of a Lunar or Martian Outpost.

The game can be adapted to shorter or longer lessons by choosing a game length of 1, 2, 3, or 4 in-game weeks.

The game also offers several levels of difficulty: (1) the Lunar Outpost features a simplified production chain, while the Martian Outpost is more complex and demanding; (2) Missions introduce three levels of difficulty (easy, normal, and difficult), placing increasing demands on production and resource management; (3) unexpected events can challenge players with module failures, astronaut injuries, disrupted production chains, and other emergencies.

We hope this game will keep you playing while learning about science and space exploration. Just as with a good book, we hope that, at the end of each game, you will say, "Let's try just one more outpost!"

Use of Artificial Intelligence

ChatGPT was used to generate most of the game's illustrations and to assist with finding and summarising NASA research and data. Production flow diagrams were designed and described by the authors and visualised using AI tools. Numerous simulated playthroughs and iterations were conducted with AI assistance, while ChatGPT was also used to analyse game balance, production ratios, and resource management, and to visualise the results.

All game design decisions and rule changes were made by the authors. AI served as a supporting tool for research, illustration, simulation, analysis, and data visualisation.
